questions.stem: The mineral fuel mined around Enugu in South-East Nigeria since the early twentieth century is
questions.explanation: Enugu is Nigeria's historic coal-mining centre; tin is associated with the Jos Plateau.

questions.stem: Cassiterite and columbite have been mined for many decades mainly on the
questions.explanation: The Jos Plateau younger granites and their alluvial deposits are the centre of Nigerian tin and columbite mining.

questions.stem: Limestone, the main raw material for cement factories at Ewekoro and Obajana, is classified as a(n)
questions.explanation: Limestone is used in industry for cement and lime, not for extraction of a metal or as a fuel.

questions.stem: Under the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007, mineral titles are applied for and granted through the
questions.explanation: The Act set up the Mining Cadastre Office to administer applications and grant of mineral titles.

questions.stem: Which of these is a mineral title provided for under the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007?
questions.explanation: Titles include reconnaissance permit, exploration licence, small-scale mining lease, mining lease, quarry lease and water use permit.

questions.stem: An association of producing countries or companies that agree to control the output and price of a mineral is a
questions.explanation: Cartels restrict supply to influence world prices; the oil producers' organisation OPEC is a well-known example.

questions.stem: A small quarry costs ₦480,000,000 to set up and is expected to earn a steady net cash inflow of ₦120,000,000 per year. Its payback period is
questions.explanation: Payback = initial investment / annual net inflow = 480 million / 120 million = 4 years.

questions.stem: The most abundant element in the Earth's crust by mass is
questions.explanation: Oxygen makes up about 46% of the crust, followed by silicon (about 28%), aluminium and iron.

questions.stem: Granite, formed by slow cooling of magma deep below the surface, is an example of
questions.explanation: Slow cooling at depth gives the coarse crystals of intrusive (plutonic) rocks like granite; basalt is extrusive.

questions.stem: When limestone is subjected to great heat and pressure deep in the crust, the metamorphic rock formed is
questions.explanation: Heat and pressure recrystallise limestone into marble; sandstone gives quartzite and shale gives slate.

questions.stem: On the Mohs scale of hardness, the mineral with hardness 7 is
questions.explanation: Talc 1, calcite 3, quartz 7, diamond 10; quartz scratches glass.

questions.stem: The breakdown of rocks in place by the action of water, oxygen and carbon dioxide, changing their mineral composition, is
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering (hydrolysis, oxidation, carbonation) alters minerals; physical weathering only breaks rock into smaller pieces.

questions.stem: The liquid layer of the Earth's interior is the
questions.explanation: Seismic S-waves do not pass through the outer core, showing it is liquid; the inner core is solid.

questions.stem: In the rock cycle, sedimentary rocks are converted into metamorphic rocks mainly by
questions.explanation: Metamorphism changes rocks in the solid state through heat and pressure; melting would form magma and then igneous rock.

questions.stem: A geologist notices that on a geological map, the oldest rocks lie in the centre of a structure and younger rocks outcrop around it in rings. The structure is most likely
questions.explanation: Erosion of an upfold (anticline/dome) exposes older rocks in the core; a syncline/basin has the youngest rocks in the centre.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: The stage of mining development that involves SEARCHING for indications of a mineral deposit over a wide area is
questions.explanation: Prospecting looks for signs of mineralisation; exploration then defines the size and grade of a discovered deposit.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Measuring variations in the Earth's magnetic field over an area to locate iron ore bodies is a
questions.explanation: Magnetic, gravity, seismic and resistivity surveys are geophysical; geochemical methods analyse soils, rocks and stream sediments.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: A feasibility study for a proposed mine is carried out to
options: determine whether the deposit can be mined technically, economically and environmentally
questions.explanation: The feasibility study assesses reserves, mining method, costs, revenue, environment and risks before investment.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: The correct order of the basic unit operations in hard-rock mining is
questions.explanation: Holes are drilled and charged, the rock is blasted, then the broken rock is loaded and hauled.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Extracting a metal from its ore by dissolving it in a chemical solution (leaching) is
questions.explanation: Hydrometallurgy uses aqueous solutions; pyrometallurgy uses heat (smelting) and electrometallurgy uses electricity.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Underground mining is usually preferred to surface mining when
options: the ore body is deep and the overburden is too thick to remove economically
the deposit lies at the ground surface
the ore is low grade and very large near the surface
large trucks and shovels must be used
questions.explanation: Deep ore bodies with high stripping costs favour underground methods; shallow, large, low-grade bodies favour surface mining.

questions.stem: A surface mine excavated as a series of benches forming a large cone-shaped pit is an
questions.explanation: Open pits deepen in benches; adits and shafts are underground access openings.

questions.stem: Open cast (strip) mining is best suited to
options: massive ore bodies 1 km below surface
flat-lying bedded deposits near the surface such as coal
questions.explanation: In open cast mining overburden is cast into the mined-out strip; it suits shallow flat seams like coal.

questions.stem: An open pit will remove 1.8 million tonnes of waste rock to obtain 0.45 million tonnes of ore. The stripping ratio is
questions.explanation: Stripping ratio = waste : ore = 1.8 / 0.45 = 4 : 1, i.e. 4 t of waste for every tonne of ore.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of operations in a granite aggregate quarry?
options: Drilling and blasting, loading and hauling, crushing, screening, stockpiling
questions.explanation: Rock is broken, transported to the crusher, crushed, sized by screens and stockpiled by size.

questions.stem: A horizontal or nearly horizontal tunnel driven from a hillside into a mine is an
questions.explanation: An adit enters from the surface on a hillside; a shaft is vertical and winzes/raises connect levels.

questions.stem: In room-and-pillar mining, pillars of ore are left in place in order to
options: support the roof of the mined-out rooms
questions.explanation: The pillars hold up the roof; some ore is therefore not recovered.

questions.stem: In shrinkage stoping, only part of the broken ore is drawn off during mining because
options: the rest is too low grade to sell
the pillars must be left permanently
the remaining broken ore is used as a working platform and to support the walls
questions.explanation: Broken rock swells; about a third is drawn off and the rest stays as a floor for miners until the stope is finished.

questions.topic: Other Mining Methods and Materials Handling
questions.stem: The deposits targeted by deep sea-floor mining that contain manganese, nickel, copper and cobalt are
questions.explanation: Potato-sized polymetallic nodules on the abyssal plains are the main proposed target of deep-sea mining.

questions.topic: Other Mining Methods and Materials Handling
questions.stem: The materials handling equipment that moves broken ore continuously on a moving belt is a
questions.explanation: Conveyors move material continuously; trucks and loaders move it in batches.

questions.stem: Crushing and grinding of ore to free the valuable mineral from the waste is called
questions.explanation: Comminution reduces particle size to liberate minerals before concentration.

questions.stem: Jigs, sluice boxes and shaking tables separate minerals mainly on the basis of differences in
questions.explanation: These are gravity concentration methods: heavy minerals such as cassiterite settle faster than light quartz.

questions.stem: The waste material discharged from a mineral processing plant after the valuable mineral has been removed is the
questions.explanation: Concentrate is the valuable product, tailings the waste, and middlings an intermediate product needing re-treatment.

questions.stem: A plant treats 100 t of tin ore assaying 2% Sn and produces 3.2 t of concentrate assaying 55% Sn. The recovery of tin is
questions.explanation: Tin in feed = 2.0 t; tin in concentrate = 3.2 x 0.55 = 1.76 t; recovery = 1.76/2.0 x 100 = 88%.

questions.stem: A rough tourmaline from Nasarawa State weighs 1.5 g. Its mass in carats (1 carat = 0.2 g) is
questions.explanation: Carats = mass in grams / 0.2 = 1.5 / 0.2 = 7.5 ct.

questions.stem: Lapidary is the art of
questions.explanation: Lapidaries cut and polish stones; gemology is the science of identifying and grading them.

questions.stem: A gemstone cut with a smooth domed top and no facets is described as
questions.explanation: Cabochons are polished domes, often used for opaque or star stones; brilliant and step cuts have facets.

questions.stem: Prolonged breathing of fine crystalline silica dust by drillers and quarry workers causes
questions.explanation: Silica dust scars the lungs, causing silicosis; dust suppression and respirators prevent it.

questions.stem: Which item of PPE allows an underground miner to see in the dark while keeping both hands free?
options: Cap lamp fixed to the safety helmet
questions.explanation: A battery cap lamp clips to the hard hat to light the working face.

questions.stem: Before a large new mining project in Nigeria is approved, the law requires an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) mainly to
options: predict and plan to reduce the effects of the project on the environment and communities
decide the selling price of the mineral
questions.explanation: The EIA identifies likely impacts such as land degradation and water pollution and sets out mitigation before approval.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of mining. [2 marks]
(b) Name the Nigerian state or area where each of the following minerals is found: (i) coal (ii) tin ore (iii) iron ore (iv) limestone (v) gold (vi) bitumen. [6 marks]
(c) State six importance of minerals to the Nigerian economy. [6 marks]
(d) Name three types of mineral title under the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The extraction of valuable minerals or other geological materials from the Earth, usually from an ore body, lode, vein, seam or placer
6 marks: (b) 1 mark each: coal - Enugu (also Kogi, Benue); tin - Jos Plateau (Plateau, Bauchi); iron ore - Itakpe/Kogi (also Agbaja); limestone - Ewekoro/Ogun, Obajana/Kogi, Nkalagu/Ebonyi, Sokoto, Cross River; gold - Zamfara, Osun (Ilesha), Niger, Kebbi; bitumen - Ondo (Agbabu), Ogun, Edo
6 marks: (c) Any six, 1 mark each: foreign exchange earnings; government revenue (royalties, taxes); employment; raw materials for industries (cement, steel); infrastructure development in mining areas; diversification of the economy; energy (coal); contribution to GDP
6 marks: (d) Any three, 2 marks each: reconnaissance permit; exploration licence; small-scale mining lease; mining lease; quarry lease; water use permit
questions.explanation: Mining is extracting valuable minerals from the earth. Coal - Enugu; tin - Jos Plateau; iron ore - Itakpe; limestone - Ewekoro/Obajana/Nkalagu; gold - Zamfara/Osun; bitumen - Ondo. Minerals give foreign exchange, revenue, jobs, industrial raw materials and diversification. Titles: reconnaissance permit, exploration licence, small-scale mining lease, mining lease, quarry lease, water use permit.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the three main classes of rock and give two examples of each. [12 marks]
(b) With the aid of a description, explain the rock cycle. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Igneous: formed by cooling and solidification of molten magma/lava (2); examples granite, basalt, gabbro, dolerite (any two, 2)
4 marks: (a) Sedimentary: formed by deposition, compaction and cementation of sediments or organic/chemical material, often layered (2); examples sandstone, shale, limestone, coal, conglomerate (any two, 2)
4 marks: (a) Metamorphic: formed by alteration of existing rocks by heat and/or pressure without melting (2); examples marble, quartzite, slate, gneiss, schist (any two, 2)
8 marks: (b) 2 marks each, any four linked stages: magma cools to form igneous rock; rocks are weathered, eroded and deposited as sediments; sediments are compacted and cemented into sedimentary rock; heat and pressure change rocks into metamorphic rock; deep burial melts rocks back into magma, completing the cycle (any rock can follow shortcuts)
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks crystallise from magma (granite, basalt); sedimentary rocks form from compacted sediments (sandstone, limestone); metamorphic rocks are altered by heat and pressure (marble, gneiss). The rock cycle: magma -> igneous -> weathering/erosion -> sediment -> sedimentary -> metamorphism -> melting -> magma.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between prospecting and exploration. [4 marks]
(b) Describe two geochemical and two geophysical prospecting techniques. [8 marks]
(c) State four factors considered in a feasibility study of a mining venture. [4 marks]
(d) Distinguish between pyrometallurgy and electrometallurgy. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Prospecting: searching an area for indications of mineral deposits using geological, geochemical, geophysical and remote sensing methods
2 marks: (a) Exploration: detailed investigation of a discovered deposit (drilling, trenching, sampling) to determine its size, shape, grade and value
4 marks: (b) Geochemical, any two, 2 marks each: stream sediment sampling; soil sampling; rock chip sampling; water/vegetation (biogeochemical) sampling - analysed for anomalous metal content
4 marks: (b) Geophysical, any two, 2 marks each: magnetic survey - variations in magnetic field (iron ores); gravity survey - density contrasts; electrical resistivity - differences in conductivity; seismic - reflection/refraction of shock waves; radiometric - radioactivity
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: size and grade of reserves; mining method and technology; capital and operating costs; mineral prices/market; infrastructure (roads, power, water); environmental and social impact; legal/title and tax regime
4 marks: (d) Pyrometallurgy: extraction using high temperature, e.g. roasting and smelting in furnaces (2); electrometallurgy: extraction/refining using electric current, e.g. electrolysis/electrowinning/electrorefining (2)
questions.explanation: Prospecting searches for signs of mineralisation; exploration defines a found deposit. Geochemical: stream sediment and soil sampling. Geophysical: magnetic, gravity, resistivity, seismic. Feasibility considers reserves, method, costs, prices, infrastructure, environment and law. Pyrometallurgy uses heat; electrometallurgy uses electricity.

questions.stem:
(a) Name and describe four underground mine openings. [8 marks]
(b) Describe the room-and-pillar method of mining and state two advantages and two disadvantages. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each: shaft - vertical/steep opening from surface for access, hoisting and ventilation; adit - horizontal tunnel into a hillside; decline/ramp - inclined tunnel for vehicles; drift/level - horizontal tunnel along the ore body; crosscut - horizontal tunnel across the ore body; raise/winze - opening between levels (driven up/down); stope - excavation where ore is mined
6 marks: (b) Description: used for flat-lying or gently dipping bedded deposits such as coal, limestone, potash (2); ore is mined in rooms in a regular pattern (2); pillars of ore are left between rooms to support the roof, some may be recovered at the end (retreat) (2)
3 marks: (b) Advantages, any two: simple and flexible; low development cost; suited to mechanisation; good ventilation; early production
3 marks: (b) Disadvantages, any two: ore in pillars is lost (low recovery); risk of roof falls/pillar failure; limited to flat-lying deposits; subsidence if pillars removed
questions.explanation: Openings: shaft (vertical), adit (horizontal from hillside), decline (inclined), drift/level, crosscut, raise/winze, stope. Room-and-pillar mines flat deposits in rooms, leaving pillars to support the roof; it is simple, cheap and mechanised, but loses ore in pillars and risks roof falls.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the following terms in mineral processing: (i) concentrate (ii) tailings (iii) middlings. [6 marks]
(b) A tin processing plant treats 500 t of ore assaying 1.2% Sn per day and produces 9.6 t of concentrate assaying 52% Sn. Calculate (i) the mass of tin in the concentrate (ii) the recovery of tin (iii) the ratio of concentration (iv) the assay of the tailings. [10 marks]
(c) Name two methods of concentration and the mineral property each uses. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) 2 marks each: concentrate - the product rich in the valuable mineral; tailings - the waste product discarded after concentration; middlings - intermediate product containing both valuable mineral and gangue, needing further treatment
2 marks: (b)(i) Tin in concentrate = 9.6 x 52/100 = 4.992 t
3 marks: (b)(ii) Tin in feed = 500 x 1.2/100 = 6.0 t; recovery = 4.992/6.0 x 100 = 83.2%
2 marks: (b)(iii) Ratio of concentration = feed/concentrate = 500/9.6 = 52.1 : 1
3 marks: (b)(iv) Tailings = 500 - 9.6 = 490.4 t containing 6.0 - 4.992 = 1.008 t Sn; assay = 0.21% Sn
4 marks: (c) Any two, 2 marks each: gravity concentration (jig, table, sluice) - specific gravity; magnetic separation - magnetic susceptibility; froth flotation - surface (hydrophobic) properties; electrostatic separation - electrical conductivity
questions.explanation: Concentrate is the valuable-rich product, tailings the waste, middlings the intermediate. Tin in concentrate = 4.992 t; recovery = 83.2%; ratio of concentration = 52.1; tailings 490.4 t at 0.21% Sn. Methods: gravity (SG), magnetic (susceptibility), flotation (surface properties), electrostatic (conductivity).

questions.stem:
(a) List four health hazards in mining and a disease or injury associated with each. [8 marks]
(b) Describe four effects of mining on the environment. [8 marks]
(c) State four items of personal protective equipment used in mines. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each (hazard + disease/injury): dust (silica/coal) - silicosis/pneumoconiosis; noise - hearing loss; heavy metals e.g. lead from ore processing - lead poisoning; toxic gases (CO, H2S) - poisoning/asphyxia; vibration - white finger; heat - heat stroke; stagnant water in pits - malaria; mercury in artisanal gold processing - mercury poisoning
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: land degradation and loss of farmland; abandoned open pits and ponds (e.g. Jos Plateau) causing drowning and erosion; water pollution from tailings and acid drainage; air pollution from dust and blasting; deforestation and loss of biodiversity; noise and ground vibration damaging buildings; subsidence over underground workings
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: safety helmet with cap lamp; steel-toe boots; dust mask/respirator; ear defenders; goggles; gloves; reflective overalls; self-rescuer
questions.explanation: Hazards: dust (silicosis), noise (hearing loss), lead and mercury (poisoning), toxic gases, heat, vibration. Environmental effects: degraded land, abandoned pits, water and air pollution, deforestation, noise/vibration, subsidence. PPE: helmet and cap lamp, boots, respirator, ear defenders, goggles, gloves, overalls, self-rescuer.
